errors.auth: {{target}} did not accept the login. Kettu logs in with your ssh-agent, the key your SSH config names for this host or the key file you chose, and cannot type a password or a key’s passphrase: put a key with a passphrase in your ssh-agent first with ssh-add. Check that {{command}} logs in without one in a terminal.

errors.noShell: {{target}} has no POSIX shell, so Kettu cannot be installed on it. The daemon runs on Linux on x64 and arm64, and on Macs with Apple silicon.
errors.not_running: Kettu is installed on {{target}}, but its daemon is not running. Run kettu service install there, or kettu run, and try again.

note.switch: Kettu checks the relay and the key before it switches. Devices online now move over at once; the others the next time they reach this computer on the same network, or when you add them again.
note.own: Only one relay at a time. Your Kettu account still sends this computer’s notifications to your iPhone.
note.pinned: The Kettu apps on computers and iPhones reach it. Browsers can’t check a pinned certificate, so they need a relay with a domain.
note.local: In Local mode Kettu sends nothing to its own services. Your relay is yours, so it stays.
note.switch_web: Kettu checks the relay and the key before it switches. Devices online now move over at once; the others the next time they reach {{host}} on the same network, or when you add them again.
note.own_web: Only one relay at a time. Your Kettu account still sends {{host}}’s notifications to your iPhone.

own.addressHint: Paste the link the relay printed when it started; its key comes with it.
own.pinnedHint: Its certificate is pinned from the link, as for a relay at an IP address.
own.keyHint: Kept on this computer only. Devices never get it.
own.keyKept: Leave it empty to keep the key ending in {{end}}.
own.refusedHint: The relay refused this computer’s access key. Paste the link it prints now under Relay.

state.noKey: No access key kept · paste the relay’s link
state.refused: Refused · the relay has a new access key

step.kettu: A Kettu relay that takes access keys

problem.address: Enter the relay’s address, such as https://relay.example.com.
problem.kettu: That’s the Kettu relay. Choose Kettu relay above to use it.
problem.http: Use https. Only a relay on this computer itself may use http.
problem.key: Enter the access key the relay printed.
problem.unreachable: Can’t reach {{host}}. Check that the relay runs and that port {{port}} is open to the internet.
problem.certificate: The certificate of {{host}} isn’t valid. A relay at an IP address prints a link with its certificate’s pin.
problem.certificatePinned: Its certificate is not the pinned one. Paste the link the relay prints now.
problem.not_kettu: This address doesn’t answer as a Kettu relay.
problem.protocol: This relay speaks another version of the relay protocol. Update the relay, or Kettu.
problem.no_access_key: This relay takes no access key. Update kettu-relay on the server.
problem.key_refused: The relay refused this key. On the relay,
problem.key_refusedEnd: prints the link with its current key.

own.keyHint_web: Kept on {{host}} only. Devices, this one included, never get it back.

discoverable.name: Let devices on your account find this computer
discoverable.description: Your devices signed in to the same Kettu account list this computer and can ask to connect. You still approve each one here.
discoverable.description_web: Your devices signed in to the same Kettu account list {{host}} and can ask to connect. You still approve each one on {{host}}.

discovery.title: Add this device?
discovery.body: {{name}} wants to connect to this computer. It is signed in to your Kettu account; add it only if you are setting it up yourself.
discovery.check: Check that the other computer shows the same code.
discovery.waiting: Waiting for {{name}} to confirm the code…

ended.stopped: The request from {{name}} ended because remote access stopped

harnesses.keywords: install update program binary cli node npm
harnesses.missingLine: Not installed. Install shows the ways {{name}}’s maker documents.

install.title: Install {{name}}
install.body: Kettu brings no {{name}} of its own: it uses the one on your computer. Pick one of {{vendor}}’s documented ways; Kettu runs it in the background and detects {{name}} again when it is done.
install.bodyPlain: Pick one of the documented ways; Kettu runs it in the background and detects {{name}} again when it is done.
install.bodyOne: Kettu brings no {{name}} of its own: it uses the one on your computer. Kettu installs it the way {{vendor}} documents, in the background, and detects {{name}} again when it is done.
install.bodyOnePlain: Kettu installs {{name}} the way its maker documents, in the background, and detects it again when it is done.
install.setupBody: Complete the requirements below to install {{name}}, then reload the environment to detect it.
install.downloadBody: Kettu downloads and installs this file for your computer.
install.ownTerminal: You can also run it in your own terminal, then come back and reload the environment.
install.cliBody: Kettu runs your own {{command}}, and brings none. Install it one of the ways its maker documents.
install.bodyCopy: Kettu installs a copy of {{name}} for you and runs it on your Node.js. If you install {{command}} yourself, Kettu uses yours first.
install.bodyCopyPlain: Kettu installs a copy of {{name}} for you and runs it on your Node.js.
install.bodyUvx: {{name}} runs through uv, which fetches it into its own cache the first time a session starts, so nothing installs now.
install.usesYours: Installs your own {{command}}, which Kettu then uses first
install.needsFirst: Install what it needs first, then reload the environment.
install.fromRegistry: {{host}}, as the ACP Registry lists it

harnesses.cliOutdated: Your {{name}} {{current}} is older than Kettu needs; update it to use it.
harnesses.cliOutdatedManual: Your {{name}} {{current}} is older than Kettu needs (at least {{minimum}}). Update it the way you installed it, then check again.
harnesses.cliUpdateBody: You have {{current}}. The update runs the way you installed {{name}}; the command shows below.
harnesses.cliUpdateBodySdk: You have {{current}}. The update runs the way you installed {{name}}, and moves Claude Agent SDK to the version that matches; the command shows below.
harnesses.reinstallBody: Delete Kettu’s install and install it again.
harnesses.programSdk: Your own, which the SDK runs.
harnesses.programKettu: Installed by Kettu, in Kettu’s data folder.
harnesses.programChosen: Picked by you, which Kettu runs.
harnesses.programUnused: Your own, which Kettu does not run.

unused.range: Your {{command}} {{version}} is outside {{range}}, the versions Kettu runs.

unused.install: Install Kettu’s own copy to use {{name}}.

harnesses.sdkLine: {{version}} · in Kettu’s data folder, without the CLI
harnesses.sdkNote: Kettu brings no {{name}}, only the SDK that drives it; updates stay within {{range}}.
harnesses.adapterNote: The adapter Kettu runs {{name}} through, on your Node.js.
harnesses.programNote: {{name}} itself, which Kettu runs on your Node.js.

autoUpdate.name: Automatic updates
autoUpdate.on: Installs the version the ACP Registry lists in the background. Running sessions keep going, and the next start uses it.
autoUpdate.off: Stays on the version it runs, and offers each new version the ACP Registry lists.
autoUpdate.wentBack: Went back from {{from}} to {{to}} {{ago}}: the ACP Registry withdrew {{from}}
autoUpdate.onKettu: Installs the version Kettu's checks recommend in the background. Running sessions keep going, and the next start uses it.
autoUpdate.offKettu: Stays on the version it runs, and offers each new version Kettu's checks recommend.
autoUpdate.wentBackBroken: Went back from {{from}} to {{to}} {{ago}}: Kettu's checks found {{from}} does not work with this version of Kettu
autoUpdate.wentBackManifest: Went back from {{from}} to {{to}} {{ago}}: Kettu's checks recommend {{to}}
autoUpdate.wentBackBundled: Went back from {{from}} to {{to}} {{ago}}: this version of Kettu comes with {{to}}
autoUpdate.noChecksum: This version has no checksum, so it can’t update automatically. Updating by hand installs it without that check.

switchBack.title: The ACP Registry withdrew {{name}} {{current}}
switchBack.body: It lists {{version}} now. Switching back installs it next to the current version unless it is still there: running sessions keep going, and {{name}} uses it from its next start.
switchBack.lineBroken: Kettu's checks recommend {{version}} in place of this version
switchBack.lineBundled: This version of Kettu comes with {{version}}
switchBack.titleBroken: {{name}} {{current}} does not work with this version of Kettu
switchBack.bodyKettu: Kettu recommends {{version}} now. Switching back installs it next to the current version unless it is still there: running sessions keep going, and {{name}} uses it from its next start.

failedVersion.title: {{name}} {{version}} did not start
failedVersion.body: Kettu went back to {{runs}} and will not install {{version}} by itself again.
failedVersion.bodyNone: Kettu will not install {{version}} by itself again.

versionWarning.unsupportedTitle: {{name}} {{version}} is outside the versions Kettu works with ({{supported}})
versionWarning.bodyUpdate: Kettu's checks found a problem with this version. Updating to {{update}} fixes it.
versionWarning.bodyRecommended: Kettu's checks passed {{recommended}}. Install that version the way you installed {{name}}, then detect again.
versionWarning.bodyOther: Install another version the way you installed {{name}}, then detect again.

uninstall.name: Uninstall {{name}}
uninstall.description: Removes what Kettu installed for it. Your own program and configuration stay.
uninstall.title: Uninstall {{name}}?
uninstall.body: Kettu deletes its installed package for {{name}} and removes the agents you added here. Any turn still running stops; their sessions stay and can still be read. Your own program, its sign-in and configuration folders are not touched.
uninstall.program: Also uninstall the program with this command
uninstall.installAgain: Install it again to use it; its configuration and sessions were kept.

switch.name: Use memory
switch.on: Every agent is handed memory when its session starts and can add to it. In Kettu’s sessions, each harness’s own memory is turned off.
switch.off: Off: each agent goes back to its own memory, as its harness keeps it.

empty.globalHint: Agents note what they learn about you as they work, and ask you before keeping it. You can add things yourself too.
empty.projectHint: Agents note how to run it, its pitfalls and decisions as they work. You can add things yourself too.
empty.noProjectsHint: Once you open a project, agents note what they learn about it as they work.

import.foundSome_other: Found {{count}} memories in the agents’ own memory
import.hint: Copy them into Kettu’s memory so every agent can use them. The originals stay as they are.

import.aboutYouHint: Tick the ones to put in global memory, which every session uses. The rest go into their project’s memory.
